clue.text: Boy precedes girl; man, woman: it's in order

definitions.text: Boy precedes girl; man, woman: it's in order

parts.words: Boy precedes girl; man, woman: it's in order
parts.note: B comes before G and M before W in the alphabet, so these pairs are listed in letter order

explanation.surface: A rule of etiquette about who goes first, boys before girls and men before women.
explanation.walkthrough: The words look like social precedence, but only their initials matter: B before G, M before W, as in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged in the sequence of the letters A to Z is said to be in this kind of order.

clue.text: Old part of fingerprint agency turned up

parts.note: an arch is one of the basic ridge patterns in a fingerprint

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue says the agency's letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: An old fragment of a print is found by an intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' sounds like 'discovered' but reverses CIA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to an earlier period, so very old.

clue.text: English learner holding up slate tablet

indicators.note: holding up in a down clue says the English learner letters sit below, supporting the word for slate

parts.note: to slate and to pan both mean to criticise harshly
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: An English student is holding a slate writing tablet aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slate' looks like a writing tablet, but it is the verb meaning criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a flat board or plaque, one sense of tablet.

clue.text: Amount's first cut accepting reduced payment

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of Amount is used
accepting says the word for cut takes the word for reduced inside

parts.note: to lance is to cut with a blade
low means reduced, as in low prices

explanation.surface: The first sum was trimmed, taking a smaller payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is a regular sum given to someone, a kind of payment.

clue.text: Aims and kills

explanation.surface: Someone takes aim and shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: purposes one strives for, and the verb for finishing someone off.

clue.text: Lag's offence receiving answer by end of sentence

indicators.note: by says the last piece sits next to the other
receiving says the word for offence takes the letter for answer inside

parts.note: an insult gives offence

indicators.note: end of says only the last letter of sentence is used

explanation.surface: A convict's crime earns a reply at the close of his prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' reads as a convict serving a sentence, but it is the verb meaning to lag pipes. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag a pipe or tank is to wrap it in material that stops heat escaping.

clue.text: Initially ascend top tread into cold room

indicators.note: Initially says the first letters of the following words are used

explanation.surface: Climb to the highest stair and into a chilly room.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room under the roof of a house.

clue.text: By seizing power becomes minister

indicators.note: seizing says the word for by holds the word for power inside

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
reach is the extent of one's power or influence

explanation.surface: A man takes power and becomes a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' suggests politics, but here it means a clergyman. 'becomes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion delivers sermons, so a clergyman who sermonises.

clue.text: Oddly, satire eases tension

indicators.note: Oddly says the first, third, fifth and other odd-placed letters are taken

explanation.surface: Strangely, a bit of satire relieves tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is strain or pressure, a synonym of tension.

clue.text: Finishes these things around day after cheating

indicators.note: after places the wrapped piece behind the word for cheating

parts.note: a con is a swindle, so cheating

indicators.note: around says the word for these things goes round the letter for day

parts.note: the setter points at the things the solver is reading: crossword clues

explanation.surface: Someone wraps things up after a bout of dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these things' is self-reference: the clues on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude something is to bring it to an end, so a verb synonym of finishes.

clue.text: Your life might be in their hands!

definitions.text: Your life might be in their hands!

parts.words: Your life might be in their hands!
parts.note: fortune-telling cards are dealt and held, and a reading claims to show your life's course

explanation.surface: A warning that your fate rests with someone, such as surgeons.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in their hands' suggests doctors or rescuers; here it is literal, a card reader holding the cards that tell your future.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack of fortune-telling cards is laid out to predict a person's future.

clue.text: Confesses, pale, head to toe

indicators.note: head to toe says the first letter of the word for pale goes to its foot

parts.note: sallow means sickly pale

explanation.surface: Someone owns up and goes white from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to toe' sounds like a description of the pallor, but it moves the S of SALLOW to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow a point is to admit or concede it, much as one confesses.

clue.text: Obstruct knife, catching clasp — one line is cut

indicators.note: catching says the shortened knife word holds the word for clasp inside
is cut says that line's letter is removed from the word for knife

parts.note: a blade is a knife
L is the abbreviation for line
a lock is a fastening or clasp

explanation.surface: A knife snags on a clasp and slices through a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cut' removes L from BLADE to leave BADE, which then holds LOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: To blockade a port or road is to block access to it, a verb synonym of obstruct.

clue.text: Old lady taking in clubs for good crack

indicators.note: taking in says the word for old lady admits a new letter
for says the letter for clubs stands in place of the letter for good

parts.note: a granny is an old lady
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Grandma takes up golf clubs and becomes a really fine player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good crack' reads as praise; 'good' is G, swapped for C, and 'crack' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small narrow opening or chink, so a crack.

clue.text: Willing adult males on island flipped

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
men are males

indicators.note: flipped says the island's name is turned round

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Grown men on an island are happy to join in.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenable means compliant or ready to agree, close to willing.

clue.text: Embroiders small person's name finally in smalls

indicators.note: in places the small person and the letter after it between the two S's

parts.note: two S's, each the abbreviation for small
a titch is a tiny person, British slang

indicators.note: finally says only the last letter of name is used

explanation.surface: A little person's name is sewn into their underwear, as on school clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smalls' is British slang for underwear, but here it gives two S's. TITCH is British slang for a small person. The 's of 'person's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing loops of thread through fabric is what embroidering does, so the verb form matches.

clue.text: Look at male trapped by work's drudgery

indicators.note: trapped by says the earlier pieces sit inside the word for work

parts.note: to till is to work the soil
to read something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A man is seen stuck in his job's grind.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'work's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a monotonous routine of tiring work, a figurative sense of drudgery.

clue.text: Divine Celia losing heart in woods

indicators.note: in places the ends of the name inside the word for woods

parts.note: a forest is woods

indicators.note: losing heart says the middle letters of the name go, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A lovely woman named Celia loses heart in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective praising Celia; it is the verb meaning foresee.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to predict by insight, as to forecast is to predict.

clue.text: Second key almost revealed master key?

indicators.note: almost says the word key loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before shortening
let on means revealed or disclosed

explanation.surface: A spare key nearly exposed the master key.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key opens many locks, the kind a master key does; the question mark flags the indirect link.

clue.text: Split from diocese about Church getting Germany's support

D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A church breaks from its diocese once Germany backs it, a Reformation scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to break away formally from a body, so to split from it.

clue.text: With destructive behaviour, idiots emptied rubbish

indicators.note: emptied says each of the three words loses its insides, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Fools behaving destructively made a mess by turning out the bins.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or fragments, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Misery capsized in distress? Send a signal

the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boat in trouble has overturned and sends out a distress call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' reads the run upwards in this down entry; no word marks the hiding apart from the letters themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is unhappiness or sorrow, a synonym of misery.

clue.text: Fakes nearly worked in cold lower regions

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the other two

parts.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth

indicators.note: nearly says the last letter of the word for worked is dropped

parts.note: a machine that ran worked

explanation.walkthrough: 'lower regions' is the underworld of Greek myth; 'Fakes' could be a verb, but the answer is a plural noun.

clue.text: Stayed in elevated hot area, saturated

elevated in a down clue says the letters read upwards

parts.note: was means stayed or remained

clue.text: Childhood disorder preceded getting confused

parts.note: ADD is attention deficit disorder, often diagnosed in children
led means went before

explanation.definitionFit: An addled mind is muddled or befuddled, a synonym.

clue.text: Further education?

parts.note: the phrase is the British name for college study after school; read as a verb, it means to gain more knowledge

explanation.surface: A reference to further education, British post-school colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: Further education is the British term for post-16 college courses; here 'Further' is the verb, so the clue asks for the act of educating oneself.

clue.text: Single that makes audible advance

parts.note: a loan is an advance of money

clue.text: Central character from 'Medea'?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Central character' suggests Medea herself; it means the middle letter, D, given its Greek name since the play is Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth letter of the Greek alphabet corresponds to D, the letter at the centre of the play's title.

clue.text: Hate to drop off — no minutes being cuddled?

indicators.note: being cuddled says those pieces are held inside the word for dropping off

parts.note: to abate is to lessen or drop off

MIN is the abbreviation for minutes

explanation.walkthrough: 'drop off' suggests sleep, but means lessen: ABATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest, a strong verb synonym.

clue.text: Caught and struck fish, in short, cut guts

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hit means struck

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the cut word
cut says the word for short loses its last letter

parts.note: terse means short or brief
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fish is caught, clubbed and quickly gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims TERSE to TERS, which holds LING. 'in short' looks like 'briefly' but supplies TERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitterlings are pig's intestines cooked as food, so guts in the culinary sense.
